lead: Billings plumbing deals with deep cold, wind, hard river water and older homes near downtown. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Billings.
risk: frozen pipes and sprinkler lines, hard water scale and aging pipes
risk_short: frozen pipes, hard water and old pipes
why: The North Side and areas near Downtown have homes from the 1900s to the 1950s with galvanized supply lines and clay sewer laterals. The West End and Heights were built mostly later.
Arctic cold snaps freeze sprinkler lines, hose bibs and pipes near exterior walls. Many homes have basements with the water heater and floor drains.
water: Billings treats water from the Yellowstone River. It is moderately hard, so scale builds up in heaters and fixtures over time.
tips: Blow out sprinkler lines before the first freeze.
Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
areas: PipeMend works Downtown and in the North Side, the Heights, the West End, Rimrock, the South Side, Briarwood and every other Billings neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Billings Building Division, and plumbers must be licensed by the Montana Board of Plumbers.

faq.a: Before the first hard freeze, often in early October. Blow out sprinkler lines, disconnect hoses and shut off outdoor faucets from inside.
